phrases: Every SQL query you've ever written is a tree.
Somewhere, something walks that tree, and turns it into rows.
Most of us never look inside.
A query execution engine, from scratch, in seven parts.
Start with one row, and one expression.
Then operators that pull rows, one at a time, up through a plan.
Join two hundred customers to five thousand orders.
A nested loop makes a million comparisons.
and finding one customer's orders goes from reading five thousand rows,
Then teach the engine to guess.
And watch exactly where the guesses go wrong.
Finally, compile the whole plan into bytecode, like SQLite does.
Working engines in Go and Closure.
